transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (Galileo Head of Security), Ethan (Galileo Platform), Sofia (Cloud Architect), Noah (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): quick security & provisioning review. Agreed pilot and follow-ups.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, I'll be the AE on this. Quick round-robin? 
00:12 Priya (Galileo Sec): Priya here, Head of Security at Galileo. We'll mainly own compliance.
00:18 Ethan (Galileo): Ethan, platform, I'll handle the integration bits.
:22 Sofia (Galileo): Sofia - cloud architecture, mainly region/data residency questions.
00:28 Liam (Redwood SE): Liam from Redwood infra, I'll walk through SAML/SCIM and RBAC patterns.
00:35 Maya: Great. The goal today is to make sure our SSO/SCIM setup meets your least-privilege model and audit requirements, and surface any blockers for a pilot.
00:50 Priya: Yep. High level: we need SOC 2/ISO artefacts, strong RBAC, audit logs exported to Splunk, and KMS or HSM for key custody. Also EU data residency for some funds.
01:10 Maya: Totally. We'll go through each. Liam, do you want to start with SAML flows and metadata?
01:18 Liam: Sure. So Redwood supports both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML. For most enterprise setups we recommend SP-initiated unless you have strict IdP flows. We accept standard SAML 2.0 metadata, certs, ACS endpoints. Small note - some customers hit mismatch on NameID format; we usually map to persistent or email based on what's in the IdP.
01:44 Ethan: On our side we'll likely use Azure AD as IdP for most teams, but a handful use Okta. Any gotchas with multiple IdPs?
01:54 Jordan (Redwood SE): You can configure multiple IdPs per account, but we need to map them to the right org unit or team. The SCIM link can be tied to a default IdP or to per-group mapping; it's configurable but it'll add complexity.
02:15 Priya: What about SAML attributes for group claims? We need to ensure groups sync for RBAC.
02:22 Liam: We usually accept group claims in either the SAML assertion or via SCIM group membership. For RBAC it's cleaner to provision groups over SCIM and base role mapping on groups.
02:35 Sofia: How does SCIM handle large orgs? We have 10k+ users across funds, groups change a lot.
02:43 Liam: SCIM v2 incremental sync is supported. We recommend delta syncs every 5-15 minutes for active environments; for very large orgs you can do hourly full syncs with deltas in between. There are rate limits; we can increase them under Dedicated or Private deployments.
03:05 Noah: Are there SCIM filters? We want to limit which users are provisioned into Redwood to only those in specific groups.
03:12 Liam: Yes, we support SCIM filtering on group membership attributes and custom attribute filters. The exact syntax depends on IdP; we provide examples for Azure/Okta/OneLogin in the docs.
03:30 Priya: And for user lifecycle - disable vs delete - we need to retain audit trails when accounts are deprovisioned.
03:38 Jordan: By default SCIM will do deprovision (user set to inactive) and we support soft-delete for 90 days in hosted. If you need longer retention or immutable audit we can route logs to your Splunk or S3 with longer retention.
04:00 Maya: Let's pivot to RBAC. Priya asked for least-privilege. Liam, what role model do you recommend?
04:08 Liam: For most customers we recommend a small set of roles: Org Admin, Team Admin, App Developer, Read-only Auditor. Then you create role slices per project. Keep business-critical permissions limited - for example model-deploy and billing are separate. We suggest a policy-based approach: roles map to groups coming from SCIM and permissions are additive.
04:34 Priya: Do you have a sample role matrix?
04:38 Liam: Yes - I'll share a template after the call. It shows least-privilege defaults and common exceptions.
04:45 Ethan: We need to make sure service accounts for CI/CD don't have deploy rights across all models. Can we bind service principals only to specific model endpoints?
04:53 Jordan: Yes - you can create scoped API keys tied to routes/models and limit by network/region. In Dedicated/Private you can also lock to VPC egress.
05:08 Priya: About audit logs: what events are logged out-of-the-box? We need at minimum auth events, token issuance, role changes, provisioning events, and model access including prompt metadata.
05:20 Liam: We log auth events, SAML assertions, SCIM provisioning and deprovision events, role changes, API key lifecycle, and request-level events. By default we redact PII and prompt bodies in hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can opt into full logging with customer-managed redaction rules.
05:38 Priya: Redaction is critical. We cannot send raw prompts with customer PII to third-party logs.
05:45 Jordan: Understood. We support both inline redaction (on ingestion) and log-shipping to your splunk with a transformation lambda to strip prompt text. We can also support tokenized hash pointers so you keep an auditable reference without sensitive content.
06:10 Sofia: For data residency - we need EU-only storage for some funds. Does Redwood have region pinning?
06:18 Liam: Yes, Redwood supports region routing. For Hosted you can pin to EU region endpoints. For strict requirements we recommend Redwood Private deployed into your VPC or on-premise, so data never leaves your network.
06:32 Noah: If we use Private, how does SAML/SCIM behave - do you still manage the control plane?
06:39 Maya: For Private deployments there's a customer-managed control plane option: some metadata still flows to Redwood for licensing but auth and logs stay in your VPC. We'll share the options doc.
06:50 Priya: KMS - do you support CMK / BYOK? We need HSM-backed keys and rotation controls.
06:56 Liam: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and can integrate with external HSMs for Private. Key rotation is supported but we recommend cadence and re-wrapping strategy. For model weights encryption vs data at rest we can separate keys.
07:18 Ethan: How are encryption keys used for logs vs model params vs S3 artifacts?
07:25 Jordan: Logs can be encrypted with your CMK in S3 or forwarded to your KMS-backed destination. Model artifacts stored in object storage can be envelope encrypted with a different CMK. We can compartmentalize keys per environment.
07:40 Priya: What about auditability for key usage - who accessed the keys?
07:45 Liam: You get key usage logs from the KMS provider. For Private deployments you can also provide HSM access logs which can be ingested into your SIEM.
07:58 Maya: Okay let's talk about a concrete pilot: scope and success criteria. Any objections?
08:05 Priya: If the pilot can demonstrate SSO + SCIM provisioning for 50 users, role mapping, and Splunk log export with redaction, we can sign off the security gate.
08:18 Ethan: We'll provide a test tenant, and a dedicated test group that should map to a "dev" role in Redwood.
08:26 Liam: We can do that. For the pilot we'll set SCIM to provision only the test group, enable SP-initiated SAML and run a smoke test of role mapping. We'll also demonstrate log shipping with prompt redaction.
08:40 Sofia: Are there sampling implications for logs? We don't want to lose traceability.
08:45 Jordan: For hosted we sample request-level logs to manage cost but we can route full fidelity to your Splunk in pilot. In Dedicated/Private you typically get full fidelity.
09:00 Priya: Anything about certification? We typically require SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 - do you have both?
09:08 Maya: Yes we have SOC 2 Type II reports and are in the process of expanding ISO scope. I'll attach the latest artifacts. Note that some reports are redacted.
09:18 Priya: Okay good. Can you also confirm retention defaults and legal hold processes?
09:24 Jordan: Hosted default logs retention is 90 days. You can extend retention in Redwood Optimize or export to your storage for longer retention. Legal hold we support via export freeze and separate archival buckets.
09:40 Priya: For some of our investments, compliance requires 7 years of some records - is that feasible via export?
09:47 Liam: Yes, via log export to your S3 or GCS bucket you can retain for 7 years. We can also provide an immutable retention policy if you need WORM-like behavior.
09:58 Noah: Slightly off-topic: how do you handle impersonation or just-in-time admin elevation? We want temporary access with approval flows.
10:06 Jordan: We offer time-bound elevated roles and can integrate with your approval workflows via webhook. We also support JIT elevation tied to SSO sessions.
10:18 Priya: Back to SCIM attribute mapping - what about custom attributes like "fund-access-level" or "sensitive-data-approval"?
10:25 Liam: SCIM supports custom extension attributes; we map them into user metadata and you can use them in policy rules. We'll show a mapping example for a custom attribute.
10:36 Ethan: Could you walk through a quick example? Maybe a mapping flow for a user who should get "Reader" in dev and "Operator" in prod?
10:44 Liam: Sure - Alice signs in and is a member of group "dev-engineers" -> SCIM provisions group membership -> Redwood maps group to role "Dev Reader" granting token-read only. For prod, a separate group maps to "Operator" with deploy permissions. We recommend different API keys and network rules per environment.
11:05 Priya: For SSO change management - when you rotate certs or update IdP config, what downtime or user impact?
11:12 Jordan: If you're careful you can support overlapping certificates (old/new) to avoid outage. We recommend a staged rotation: upload new cert and keep old cert active for two weeks, then remove old. For SCIM we support replay-safe updates so minimal churn.
11:30 Sofia: Any gotchas for Azure AD specifically?
11:34 Liam: Azure tends to send large group claims. If they exceed assertion size we recommend group provisioning via SCIM rather than in assertion. Also Azure sometimes uses immutableId mapping - we'll document attribute mappings.
11:50 Priya: About role audits - do you provide tooling to show who has what permissions historically?
11:56 Liam: We maintain role change history and can supply an export that shows role grants, who approved, and timestamps. For locked-down audits we also produce signed event manifests.
12:12 Maya: Great. Let's surface any risks or red flags. Priya?
12:17 Priya: Main risk is accidental exposure of full prompt text. The proposed redaction approach and export to our Splunk should mitigate that. Also need clarity on export encryption in transit.
12:27 Jordan: Exports are TLS 1.2+ and we support mutual TLS for delivery endpoints.
12:34 Ethan: Another concern: SCIM rate limits interfering with large provisioning windows. You mentioned raising caps on Dedicated - what's the timeline?
12:42 Liam: We can raise rate limits immediately for pilot; for production scale we'll size Dedicated pool or Private.
12:52 Sofia: Any legal holds or eDiscovery features in Redwood?
12:56 Jordan: We support flagged records and snapshot export for eDiscovery. We'll coordinate with legal.
13:06 Priya: Alright. Can you summarize the concrete next steps?
13:10 Maya: Yes - exchange SAML metadata and SCIM creds, Redwood send SOC2/ISO artifacts, Liam share RBAC template, schedule pilot.
13:20 Ethan: I'll get metadata to you by Friday.
13:24 Maya: Great. Anything else?
13:28 Priya: One last thing - will you redact prompt text in logs by default for the pilot?
13:35 Liam: For the pilot we'll enable redaction by default and show you the transformation. If you want to see full prompts in a controlled environment we can spin up Private pilot in your VPC.
13:48 Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone.
13:56 Priya: Thanks.
14:00 Meeting end.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Pilot defined: SSO (SP-initiated), SCIM provisioning for test group (~50 users), RBAC mapping sample, Splunk log export with redaction.
- Compliance docs to be shared by Redwood (SOC2 type II, ISO scope)
- Logs retention export required for 7-year archival for some funds (Galileo to confirm which records).
- Redwood to provide RBAC matrix and SCIM mapping examples.
